bugs.title: World generation bugs
bugs.lead: Why does a Burial Chamber on my seed have other rooms than on a friend's, on the very same seed? Because the game turns each Burial Chamber at random, apart from the seed, and the turn decides its rooms.

crypts.title: Burial Chambers differ on the same seed
crypts.how: The game sets every location down at one of {yaws} turns, {step}° apart, and picks the turn with a random number that the seed does not fix. For most locations the turn changes nothing inside. A Burial Chamber in the Black Forest is different: the turn shifts its dungeon's generator a little, and the generator's position becomes the seed of the dungeon's rooms.
crypts.cores: So one Burial Chamber on one seed has a few possible layouts, each with its own rooms, chests and surtling cores. Which one a world gets is settled when the chamber is first generated, and stays.
crypts.others: Sunken Crypts, troll caves, Infested Mines and the other dungeons are not touched by it: their rooms follow from the seed alone.
crypts.maps: A seed map that shows a single layout for a Burial Chamber shows one of its possible layouts. What a world really holds is in its save, once someone has walked in.

guides.title: Guides
guides.start: Where do I go first on a new seed? Read Where to go first on a new seed: the Meadows and Eikthyr, then the Black Forest with copper and tin, and what each stage can and cannot skip.

start.title: Where to go first on a new seed
start.lead: Where do I go first on a new seed? Through the Meadows to Eikthyr's altar, a short walk from the start, then into the Black Forest to a troll cave near the shore, with copper at its entrance and tin on the beach below.

meadows.title: The Meadows: Eikthyr
meadows.why: Eikthyr's hard antler is what the first pickaxe is made of, and without a pickaxe there is no copper and no tin.
meadows.near: On half of all seeds his altar is within {median} m of the start; on nine seeds in ten within {most} m.
meadows.island: On {island}% of seeds it stands on the start island. On the rest it is across water, so the first boat comes before the first boss.
meadows.skip: Technically you can walk past him, but not on a run: no antler means no pickaxe and no bronze, and his power, which cuts what running and jumping cost in stamina, carries half the game.
meadows.bees: Bees come from beehives in the Meadows' abandoned houses, each house holding one at a {chance}% chance: a run needs three for mead, four on a speedrun. The third nearest hive is usually {third} m from the start, the fourth {fourth} m.

blackForest.title: The Black Forest: copper, tin and the first home
blackForest.near: The start sits in a ring of Meadows: the nearest Black Forest is usually {median} m away, and rarely nearer than {least} m.
blackForest.island: On {island}% of seeds the start island has Black Forest of its own.
blackForest.why: Settle at a troll cave: the ledge at its mouth is flat ground, which the Black Forest rarely gives, and two copper veins by the entrance is the sign to stop there.
blackForest.caves: Of the {all} troll caves nearest the start, usually {caves} have two copper veins or more within reach of the entrance; the nearest of them is usually {nearest} m from the start.
blackForest.walk: The whole way of the first days — start, Eikthyr, that cave — is usually {walk} m.
blackForest.tin: Tin grows only at the water's edge. Within {reach} m of that cave there are usually {tin} tin deposits, and the cave is usually {shore} m from the sea: copper and tin in one trip, and the boat at the door.
